title: Yudhishthira Chooses Nakula
text:
During their exile in the forest, the five Pandava brothers grew desperately thirsty. Nakula went looking for water and found a clear lake. A voice warned him not to drink until he had answered its questions. He ignored it, drank, and fell dead. Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima followed one by one and met the same fate.

Last came Yudhishthira, the eldest. He found his four brothers lying lifeless at the water's edge. The voice, a yaksha, a nature spirit, posed its riddles, and Yudhishthira answered every one patiently and wisely: what is faster than the wind (the mind), what is the greatest wonder (that people see others die every day and still act as if they will live forever).

Pleased, the yaksha offered to bring back one brother. Yudhishthira chose Nakula. The yaksha was astonished: why not mighty Bhima or the great archer Arjuna, on whom he would depend in war?

Yudhishthira explained that his father had two wives, Kunti and Madri. He himself was Kunti's son and still alive. If Nakula lived, Madri too would have a son left. He would not favor his own mother's line. The yaksha then revealed himself as the god Dharma, Yudhishthira's own father, and restored all four brothers to life.
lesson: Fairness means looking after the people who have the least standing, even when favoring your own side would be easier or more useful.
people: Yudhishthira, the Yaksha (Dharma), Nakula, Bhima, Arjuna, Sahadeva
source: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the Yaksha Prashna episode
